2608.26860.title: Reinforcement Learning-Based Control of CAV Platoon Joining Maneuvers in Mixed Traffic
2608.26860.paper_summary: Connected and automated vehicle (CAV) platooning offers a promising approach to improving road safety and traffic capacity. However, platoon control in real-world traffic is challenging due to uncertainty and heterogeneous driving behaviors. Reinforcement learning (RL) has strong potential for addressing such control problems, but its practical deployment raises challenges related to safety and learning efficiency. This paper proposes a generic modeling and simulation framework for investigating CAV platoon joining maneuvers and comparing deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based control algorithms. The problem is particularly challenging in mixed-traffic environments, where CAVs coexist with human-driven vehicles exhibiting heterogeneous longitudinal and lateral behaviors. The objective is to achieve safe and efficient joining maneuvers by either incorporating penalties for risky behaviors into the learning process or using an external safety controller to constrain the learned policy. An agent-based modeling framework coupled with the Simulation of Urban MObility (SUMO) simulator is used to evaluate Deep Q-Network (DQN), Double Deep Q-Network (DDQN), and Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO). Results show that PPO outperforms DQN and DDQN, achieving a joining success rate of approximately 98 % and a collision rate below 1 %, largely due to risk-related penalties incorporated into the reward function. However, this improved performance requires more decision steps to complete the maneuver, revealing a trade-off between safety, joining effectiveness, and decision efficiency. An external safety controller effectively prevents collisions, although its interventions may reduce joining efficiency. The results highlight the importance of jointly considering safety and efficiency when designing RL-based controllers for CAV platoon joining in mixed traffic.
2608.26860.paper_summary_zh: 連結與自動化車輛（CAV）編隊提供了一種改善道路安全和交通容量的有前景的方法。<lb/>然而，在現實交通中進行編隊控制具有挑戰性，因為存在不確定性和異質的駕駛行為。<lb/>強化學習（RL）在解決此類控制問題方面具有很大的潛力，但其實際部署帶來了與安全性和學習效率相關的挑戰。<lb/>本文提出了一個通用的建模和模擬框架，用於研究CAV編隊加入操作並比較基於深度強化學習（DRL）的控制算法。<lb/>在混合交通環境中，這個問題尤其具有挑戰性，因為CAV與展現異質縱向和橫向行為的人駕駛車輛共存。<lb/>目標是通過將對風險行為的懲罰納入學習過程，或使用外部安全控制器來約束學習策略，來實現安全且高效的加入操作。<lb/>一個基於代理的建模框架與城市移動模擬（SUMO）模擬器相結合，用於評估深度Q網絡（DQN）、雙深度Q網絡（DDQN）和近端政策優化（PPO）。<lb/>結果顯示，PPO的表現優於DQN和DDQN，實現了約98%的加入成功率和低於1%的碰撞率，這主要歸功於納入獎勵函數的風險相關懲罰。<lb/>然而，這種改進的性能需要更多的決策步驟來完成操作，顯示出安全性、加入有效性和決策效率之間的權衡。<lb/>外部安全控制器有效地防止了碰撞，儘管其干預可能會降低加入效率。<lb/>這些結果突顯了在設計基於RL的CAV編隊加入控制器時，聯合考慮安全性和效率的重要性。
